Apollo

Apollo is a reliable, centralized configuration management system designed for microservice and distributed application scenarios. It provides unified management of configurations across different environments, clusters, and applications with real-time hot-release capabilities. The system includes a server component built on Spring Boot and Spring Cloud, along with SDKs for Java and .NET that integrate seamlessly with various runtime environments.

🕐 Generated August 28, 2026 at 12:56 AM UTC
Technology Stack: Spring Boot 4.0.5 Spring Cloud 2025.1.1 Spring Cloud Alibaba 2025.1.0.0 Spring Data JPA Jakarta Mail Apache HttpClient 4.5.14 Guava 32.0.0 Apache Commons Lang3 3.18.0 Javassist 3.23.1-GA
Apollo is organized into a layered, modular architecture with clear separation of concerns: Controllers expose REST APIs for managing configurations (apps, clusters, namespaces, releases, items); Services coordinate business logic across repositories and domain entities; Repositories provide data access via Spring Data JPA; Entities represent core domain objects with soft-delete support and audit tracking. Cross-cutting concerns are handled through AOP aspects (namespace locking, audit span capture), servlet filters (authentication), and HTTP interceptors. The system includes audit logging with distributed tracing support, gray release management with rule caching, message-based release notification, and database-backed service discovery and registry components. Configuration is managed through Spring Boot auto-configuration with feature toggles for audit logging and service registry functionality.
Domain Modules: Application Management Namespace and Cluster Configuration Release Management and Gray Deployments Configuration Items (Key-Value Pairs) Audit Logging and Tracing Access Control and Authentication Service Discovery and Registry Release Messaging and Notifications

Multiple cache-related properties suggest a sophisticated caching strategy with configurable scan and rebuild intervals. Includes length and count limits for keys, values, items, and namespaces with per-app and per-namespace overrides, indicating multi-tenant support. parseOverrideConfig method has elevated cyclomatic complexity (6), suggesting complex conditional logic for configuration parsing and validation.

Conditional configuration pattern: Uses @ConditionalOnProperty to activate only when audit logging is explicitly enabled, preventing overhead when disabled. Composition over inheritance: Aggregates multiple specialized services (LogService, DataInfluenceService, TraceContext) into a unified ApolloAuditLogApi facade. Aspect-oriented design: Employs AspectJ aspect and HTTP interceptor for non-invasive audit instrumentation across application layers. Extension points: Provides @ConditionalOnMissingBean for ApolloAuditOperatorSupplier and ApolloAuditLogQueryApiPreAuthorizer to allow custom implementations.

Null Object pattern: Provides no-op implementations of all audit components to avoid null checks and enable graceful feature degradation when audit logging is disabled. Complementary configuration: Works in tandem with ApolloAuditAutoConfiguration using mutually exclusive @ConditionalOnProperty conditions (enabled=false vs enabled=true). Defensive bean registration: Uses @ConditionalOnMissingBean extensively to ensure no-op beans are only registered if the active configuration hasn't already provided real implementations. Symmetric API surface: Maintains the same bean contract as the enabled configuration, allowing downstream code to operate identically regardless of audit state.

MethodDescription
ConfigChangeContentBuilder createItem(Item item) Adds a new item to the list of created items and returns this builder for method chaining.
ConfigChangeContentBuilder updateItem(Item oldItem, Item newItem) Records a change from an old item to a new item in the updates list and returns this builder for method chaining.
ConfigChangeContentBuilder deleteItem(Item item) Adds an item to the list of deleted items and returns this builder for method chaining.
boolean hasContent() Checks whether any configuration changes (creates, updates, or deletes) have been recorded.
String build() Serializes all recorded configuration changes into a JSON string representation.
Item cloneItem(Item source) Creates a deep copy of an Item object.
ConfigChangeContentBuilder convertJsonString(String content) Parses a JSON string and populates the builder's change lists from the parsed content, returning this builder for method chaining.
List getCreateItems() Returns the list of items that have been recorded as created.
List getUpdateItems() Returns the list of item pairs that have been recorded as updated.
List getDeleteItems() Returns the list of items that have been recorded as deleted.
Implements the builder pattern for fluent API allowing chainable configuration change tracking Handles bidirectional conversion between object representation and JSON serialization of config changes
